label.verdict_reason: It is a syntax reference (four ways to write a test, how $? works) you look up, not reasoning or a story.

key_ideas.text: Bash offers four kinds of test: the test command / single brackets, shell arithmetic (( )), the double-bracket extended test [[ ]], and functions, commands or programs used as tests.
A single bracket is a command, so it needs a space after [ and before ]; omitting it concatenates the bracket with the next token and fails with "command not found".
Any command's exit status of 0 means true and any non-zero status means false in Bash, which is the reverse of how many other languages read true/false.
$? holds the exit status of the last command, and reading it (even with echo) resets it, so a value you need must be captured into a variable before the next command runs.
[[ ]] does not require double-quoting its left operand the way [ ] does, because word splitting and filename expansion are not performed inside [[ ]].
